body:
did you know the most quietly devastating song on evermore is in a time signature almost nobody writes pop in?

aaron dessner built the piano part for "tolerate it" in 10/8 — an odd, lopsided meter he almost didn't send taylor, because he thought it was too experimental. she wrote to it anyway. that off-kilter pulse is *why* the song always sounds like it's holding its breath.

and the story on top of it didn't even start in her own life. taylor has said she was reading daphne du maurier's "rebecca," fixed on a husband who merely tolerates a wife trying desperately to please him — and folded a feeling she'd known herself into it. track five, of course. the slot she saves for the song that hurts the most.

(if you've seen the eras tour: it's the one at the candlelit dinner table set for two.)

longlivets.com
why: Did-you-know track-fact pillar — deliberately a craft/lore fact, not a chart record (the last two did-you-knows were both chart records: ATW 10-min, adult-contemporary). Pulls from the thinly-covered evermore era. Every claim is confirmed-tier in the vault evermore track dossier (tolerate-it): Dessner wrote the piano part in 10/8 and almost didn't send it (too experimental); Taylor confirmed the Rebecca / du Maurier inspiration directly (Apple Music, Dec 2020); track five = the slot she reserves for her most vulnerable song; the Eras candlelit dinner-table-for-two staging. Music/craft lore only — outside every blocklist topic. Scheduled 07-29 to fill the cadence gap after the 07-28 Midnights item. Media: /eras/evermore.png (committed era tile).
